title: Myanmar’s Resistance Finally Has a Unified Front
gist: First-person account by Zaw Wai Soe, former Dean of the University of Medicine in Yangon, who became an underground resistance activist after Myanmar's February 2021 coup, fled into exile, and was appointed minister of health and education in the National Unity Government (NUG) formed in April 2021 to lead the anti-coup resistance.

themes.theme: From academic to exiled resistance leader

insights.claim: Zaw Wai Soe was serving as Dean of the University of Medicine in Yangon when Myanmar's military staged its coup in February 2021, after which he became an activist in the resistance movement overnight, serving in a variety of roles.
insights.speaker: Zaw Wai Soe
insights.so_what: Illustrates how Myanmar's February 2021 coup rapidly pulled established professionals and academics into active resistance roles, a pattern relevant to understanding the depth and composition of anti-junta opposition.
insights.quote: I was serving as Dean of the University of Medicine in Yangon when Myanmar’s military staged its coup in February 2021. Overnight, I became an activist in the resistance movement, serving in a variety of roles.
insights.locator: I was serving as Dean of the University

insights.claim: Zaw Wai Soe joined peaceful protests and helped lead the Civil Disobedience Movement, which made him a wanted man, forcing him to flee first to a neighboring country and eventually to seek refuge in Europe.
insights.speaker: Zaw Wai Soe
insights.so_what: Shows the personal risk and displacement faced by Myanmar's resistance leadership, useful for gauging the human capital cost and exile-based structure of the opposition movement.
insights.quote: My involvement soon made me a wanted man, forcing me to flee to a neighboring country before I eventually received refuge in Europe.
insights.locator: My involvement soon made me a wanted man

themes.theme: The National Unity Government's institutional role

insights.claim: Zaw Wai Soe was appointed minister of health and education in Myanmar's National Unity Government (NUG), which was formed in April 2021 to lead the resistance to the military coup.
insights.speaker: Zaw Wai Soe
insights.so_what: Confirms the NUG's ongoing function as a parallel government structure with functioning ministries, relevant for assessing its legitimacy and operational capacity as an opposition authority.
insights.quote: I was later appointed minister of health and education in the National Unity Government (NUG), which was formed in April 2021 to lead the resistance to the coup.
insights.locator: I was later appointed minister of health

insights.claim: As of April 2026, the National Unity Government's Defense Ministry was running civil-defense capacity-building training programs, evidenced by a graduation ceremony for trainees in Sagaing Region, Myanmar.
insights.speaker: Zaw Wai Soe
insights.so_what: Indicates the NUG continues to build organized military/civil-defense capacity more than five years into the conflict, a sign of sustained institutional resilience worth tracking against the junta's control.
insights.quote: Civil defense trainees attend a graduation ceremony for a capacity building program run by the Defense Ministry of Myanmar’s National Unity Government in Sagaing Region, Myanmar, Apr. 19, 2026.
